summary: Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Hermann Grassmann and at Greifswald, Strasbourg, and Tübingen (PhD ~1876). He taught at Kriegsschule Dresden (~1876–1881) and edited for Open Court and The Monist (~1887–1919).

Paul Copp specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at UMass Amherst and Princeton (PhD attested 2005 under Stephen F. Teiser), he held positions at Western Michigan University, the Heidelberg Academy (2006), and the University of Chicago (attested 2014, 2026).

Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who completed graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer. He served as a professor at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Devanandan was a religious studies scholar educated at Nizam College, Presidency University, Pacific School of Religion, and Yale (doctorate ~1931). He taught at Jaffna College, served as professor at United Theological College (1932–1949), and directed CISRS (1956).

Paul David Numrich is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Michigan in 1992. In 2006, he held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Debes was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954, also serving as a board member), the journal Wissen und Wandel (1955), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955).

Paul Demiéville was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi, Paul Pelliot, and Édouard Chavannes across several Paris institutions. His appointments included EFEO, Xiamen University, Maison Franco-Japonaise, INALCO, EPHE (1945–1957), and Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin under Christian Lassen. He held posts at RWTH Aachen (~1879–1881), Humboldt University of Berlin (1881–1887), and Kiel University as professor (1889).

Paul Dundas was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He led Asian studies at the University of Edinburgh (~1976–2017) and also served as head of the Pali Text Society.

Paul E. Muller-Ortega is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was a doctoral student at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He taught in the Department of Religion and Classics at the University of Rochester (attested 2000).
Paul Ekman studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held a post at the University of California, San Francisco, from approximately 1960 to 2004.

Paul F. Knitter is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University and the University of Marburg. He held a post at Union Theological Seminary around 2007.

Paul Fredericq was a historian who studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège (doctorate ~1875). He served as a professor at the University of Liège (~1879–1883) and at Ghent University (from 1883), where he became rector in 1919.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Paul Dundas and Rupert Gethin, earning his PhD from the University of Bristol. He holds a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Paul G. Hackett is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as South Asia Bibliographer and Tibetan Collection curator at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and later held research and lecturing posts at Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Akira Hirakawa at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Yale. He has served as a faculty member and professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2026).

Paul Hacker was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate from Berlin (~1940) and habilitated at Bonn (1949). He held posts at Münster, the Mithila Institute, the University of Pennsylvania, and chaired Indology at Bonn (1955–1963) and Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Auckland and the Australian National University (PhD ~1979) under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He taught at ANU, Auckland, Canterbury, and joined Stanford University's faculty (~2007).
Paul Hoornaert is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held teaching posts at Kanazawa University, attested in 1991 as lecturer and in 2002.

Paul J. Griffiths is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Oxford and Wisconsin (PhD 1983). He held faculty posts at Wisconsin, Chicago, Notre Dame, UIC (2000–2007), and Duke University (~2007–2017).
